findings.note: ELITEA-2343's case text (step 6, 'Click the crossed-out eye icon') could in principle be misread as referring to the three-dot menu's 'Hide' item instead of the row-level eye-icon toggle, since both exist on the same row. Checked via dedup: sibling case ELITEA-2344 / issue #852 already exists specifically to cover the three-dot menu's server-side Hide mutation, and ELITEA-2343's own steps 3-8 confirm the row-level toggle is the focus (step 1's navigation, steps 2–8 assertion chain). No AFS amendment needed — the case intent is clear. Case text might be clarified for future re-readers: 'Click the eye icon at the row's end' → 'Click the eye-icon visibility toggle on the row.'

Discovered that @mui/icons-material icon components carry an auto-generated data-testid={ExportName} on their <svg> with zero app-authored data-testid prop (confirmed live via browser_evaluate + confirmed in SecretsTable.jsx source that neither <VisibilityIcon> nor <VisibilityOffIcon> is given one at the call site). Used this as a scoped, testid-shaped sub-selector for icon-state verification, expecting it would be reliable. Later discovered it is dev-build-only: MUI's createSvgIcon.js gates the auto-testid on `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, so VisibilityIcon/VisibilityOffIcon data-testid is undefined on any deployed/production build. This blocks the test on any non-dev environment.

secrets_page.py's existing open_row_actions_menu() carries a documented declared-improvisation React-onClick-direct-invoke workaround because a normal Playwright click allegedly could never open the three-dot MUI Menu (ELITEA-2338 implementation-day finding, deterministic across many trials). This session, a plain browser_click on the same button opened the menu successfully on the first attempt (and consistently thereafter in verification runs). The finding may be stale or environment-specific; documented but not removed pending further investigation by a dev with Playwright deep-knowledge.

Known defect #1203 (React 'Maximum update depth exceeded' on /settings/secrets mount) fired deterministically this run (21 occurrences) — confirmed still OPEN. Soft-asserted per the sanctioned-RED pattern (.agents/testing.md § Merge gate), same idiom as the merged ELITEA-2338 test. No new defect found.

Declared improvisation preserved from the AFS: the icon-state sub-selectors (VISIBILITY_ICON_VISIBLE_SELECTOR / VISIBILITY_ICON_HIDDEN_SELECTOR) key off MUI's own vendor-auto-generated data-testid on the icon <svg> children, chained off the new app testid. Both branches are exercised by this test's own steps (reveal + hide), matching canon ruling #277's 'both branches referenced' shape. Flagged for review as a #579-scoped-raw-handle exception (third-party internals of @mui/icons-material — the ExportName auto-testid is library-internal, not app JSX).

Git process incident: committed directly onto the batch trunk (tests/batch-elitea-2343-secret-eye-icon-reveal) instead of a feature branch, 5th recorded recurrence of this exact pipeline-wide mistake. Recovered via revert+cherry-pick without any force-push touching shared trunk history — full recovery runbook now appended to .agents/memory/test-automation-engineer/verify_feature_branch_before_first_commit.md for future reference.

CRITICAL / blocking. The icon-state sub-selectors `VISIBILITY_ICON_VISIBLE_SELECTOR`/`VISIBILITY_ICON_HIDDEN_SELECTOR` (`[data-testid="VisibilityIcon"]`/`[data-testid="VisibilityOffIcon"]`), used by `expect_visibility_icon_masked_state()`/`expect_visibility_icon_revealed_state()` and asserted in test Steps 3, 6 and 9, rely on MUI's `createSvgIcon()` internal — verified in EliteaUI's own `node_modules/@mui/material/utils/createSvgIcon.js` line 48: `'data-testid': process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? (name || 'SvgIcon') : undefined`. On localhost/dev (NODE_ENV=development), the auto-testid renders. On any deployed env (production build), it is undefined. The test passes on localhost and fails hard on DEV/next/prod. BLOCKER: cannot land without fixing.

Non-blocking. Step 8's value-cell recheck uses `value_cell.text_content() == masked_value` (a raw synchronous read, no retry/wait) instead of `expect(value_cell).to_have_text(...)`, even though Step 5 and the equivalent check embedded in Step 7's block both correctly use `expect(...).to_have_text(...)`. Not currently racy — the wait already happened inside Step 7's block right before this — but it is inconsistent and fragile.

Nit. `SECRET_REVEAL_URL_SUBSTRING = "/secrets/secret/default/"` in the test file duplicates the identical string already defined as `SECRET_DELETE_URL_SUBSTRING` in `automation/pages/secrets_page.py` (module-level, importable). Minor DRY issue — not blocking, but worth importing the existing constant instead of re-literalizing the URL substring in a second place.
